entry.title: Herbal 0.1.0
entry.content:
Herbal 0.1.0: the first release.
A small offline book of herbs for tea, for the Mudita Kompakt.
- 44 herbs, A to Z, each with what it is traditionally used for and what the research says, how to brew it (°F and °C), the plant, its cautions and its sources. An herb with a serious caution says so at the top of its page. Four "don't use" pages say why not. - A finder by everyday need: sleep, calm, digestion, colds, sore throat, nausea, headache, period cramps, pregnancy and nursing. - A brew timer with green and black tea, herbal infusion, decoction and settings of your own. It rings with the screen off. - A journal of what you brewed, and a cupboard of what you have. - The journal, cupboard and your own timer settings can be kept as one file and read back in.
No account, no network: there is no internet permission. It is a reference book, not medical advice.

entry.title: Home 1.0.0
entry.content:
# Home 1.0.0
Home is a plain, quiet home screen for E Ink phones, made on the Mudita Kompakt. It is [inkOS](https://github.com/gezimos/inkos) by gezimos, as its own app beside inkOS, with what the apps made to work with it need. Everything inkOS does still works, and a backup from inkOS restores into Home.
- **One Nextcloud account for the whole phone.** Sign in once, in the first run or in Settings → Nextcloud account. The apps that sign in to Nextcloud get a row "Use the phone's Nextcloud account": one tap there, and nothing to type. The password is locked on the phone and handed only to those apps, checked by their signing key. Signing out in Home signs them out too and deletes the password on the server. - **Your apps.** Settings → Your apps lists the apps made to work with Home, in folders (Core first), each one installed or missing, with Install and Update. A download is installed only if its size, checksum, package, version and signing key are the right ones. With no connection it shows the list Home carries, without installing. - **Settings in groups**: Phone, Apps, Home screen, Setup and about, in the same plain look as the other apps. inkOS's own pages and rows are all still there. - **Dark mode for all the apps.** On MuditaOS, Settings → Dark mode turns Home dark, and the other apps follow it. On other phones, Home follows the phone's own dark setting. - **A first run of its own**: welcome and privacy, setup, your apps, default apps, Nextcloud, theme and home apps. Settings → Run setup again opens it again; nothing is reset. - **Default apps.** One row for each kind of thing the apps open: calls, texts, contacts, calendar, alarms, gallery, maps, text files, passwords and more. Each row says what Android does today. - **Lines on home.** Up to three lines under the home apps from [Glance](https://github.com/wanderwildwood/hitome) 0.1.24 or later: today's events, the weather, what is unread. A press opens the app the line came from; a long press shows each source and what it is doing. The lines can sit at the top or at the bottom. - Also: music on the lock screen for any player, folders in the app drawer, E-ink mode per app on MuditaOS 2.0 and later, a contact found in search opens in Connections, all-day events show on their own date, and service notifications no longer badge their apps.
Unlike inkOS, Home has the internet permission, used only for Your apps and for your own Nextcloud server. Home has no server of its own and sends nothing about you.
1.0.0 installs over a 0.1.0 test build and keeps its settings.
Nearly all of Home is inkOS, by [gezimos](https://github.com/gezimos), under the GPL-3.0. Thank you. For plain inkOS, go to [gezimos's repository](https://github.com/gezimos/inkos).

entry.title: Messaging 1.35.44
entry.content:
# Messaging 1.35.44
- A passphrase lock, off unless you turn it on (Settings, Display, Passphrase lock). While locked, Signal messages and calls wait until you unlock, Desktop Sync stops, and a text shows only that something arrived; it is brought into the app when you unlock. It locks when the screen turns off, a set time after you leave the app, or when you choose Lock now, never during a call. If the passphrase is forgotten, the only way back is to clear the app's data and link Signal again - When the lock closes, the memory the app used is overwritten, so nothing read can be recovered from it (can be turned off) - Backups are encrypted with a 30-digit backup code, made once and shown for writing down; no backup is made without one. To restore on another phone, enter that phone's code first. Older backups still restore - Automatic backups, daily or weekly, keeping the newest 1 to 10 - The backup location row names the folder in use - An optional SOCKS proxy for Signal (Settings, Signal), for example Orbot for Tor. Signal calls are off while it is on, because they cannot go through it - In a conversation with disappearing messages, call lines disappear with the messages - Signal's encryption library is updated to 0.108.0, as Signal Android uses it
## Fixed
- An edit of a view-once message no longer makes its picture last - Settings no longer stops responding when many Signal updates arrive at once

entry.content:
# Tuner 0.1.53
- A readout to tune by: below the strings, the note in large type, how many cents flat or sharp with which way to turn, and a scale from −50 to +50 cents with a dot where the pitch sits - The reading holds still on a held note: it shows the middle of each half second's readings and redraws only when that moves three cents or more - When the string dies away the last reading stays, grayed, until another note is aimed at - In tune also says by how many cents - The pitch graph is a tap away: a tap on the readout shows the graph in its place, a tap on the graph brings the readout back, and the choice is remembered

entry.title: Shelf 0.1.40
entry.content:
# Shelf 0.1.40
- The bar with Scan and Shelf order is the same height as the other apps' top bars - Spreadsheet export keeps every text cell from running as a formula, and a book known only by its LCCN survives the round trip - A QR sign-in is checked with the server before it is kept - Books found without the Library of Congress are looked up there again quietly, two a minute and never ahead of a fresh scan; with no connection, the asking waits for one to come back - The tabs always fit across the screen - Listen asks only the real Audio Reader, before a title goes out or a book is opened - Dark mode and the file picker trust only the real Home and Cabinet apps; once Home is removed, the app's own dark setting applies again, and it keeps its last setting while Home is briefly unavailable, as during its update
## Fixed
- Sync compares files from a compressing web server as the same file - An unreadable catalog is kept aside, and a failed write no longer closes the app - Nothing is saved, synced or imported until the library has loaded, and a book added meanwhile is kept - Import matches a row known by its LCCN alone, so books still waiting for a lookup no longer hide it as already here - A Dewey number with a stray mark is saved clean and no longer crashes Sections - A lookup only the unreachable catalogs might know is a miss, not tried every minute - Genre fill with a catalog out of reach waits for the next start instead of ending for good - A tap on the scrollbar lands on the right row after the screen changes

entry.title: Atlas 0.1.15
entry.content:
# Atlas 0.1.15
- Follow trail: Walk to here follows a trail from where you meet it to the spot marked on it, kept across restarts; away from the trail, Walk to the trail plans a walking route to its nearest point - Walk to here has its own icon: a walking figure with a flag ahead - Dark mode reaches the wait dialogs for moving maps and sharing or importing bookmarks; the streamed map and the OpenStreetMap profile picture keep their colors - Own-server dialogs say that a plain http:// address is taken for a server at home, and is sent unencrypted - A contact's address tapped into the search, or used for directions from the place screen, is not kept in the search history - A bug report carries the phone's system information as text in the mail rather than the app's log, and log archives left by earlier reports are deleted - Place types use US English (Highway, not Motorway); British and New Zealand English keep Motorway - Bookmark notes load nothing from the network, so a picture in an imported note does not tell its server the place was opened - Dark mode takes Home's switch only from the real Home app, and the app's own setting applies again once Home is removed; it keeps its last setting while Home is briefly unavailable, as during its update
## Fixed
- Walk to here starts from a fresh, close position, stops on the pass of the trail that was marked, and finds the marked spot on a trail made of several lines; deleting the followed track ends following - An online address lookup tries Photon when the Census geocoder cannot be reached - Fastest for one trip no longer turns off avoid-motorways set in Settings - On a phone that turns sideways, the navigation and downloader panels no longer close the app - Another app can no longer plan a route through the map's own extras, or close the app with a bookmark or track that is gone - Search asks Contacts off the main thread as you type - A tap on the scrollbar lands on the right row after the screen changes
